# Which startup methods must be prohibited when transitioning from simulation to real hardware in Legged-Control?

> **Current answer:** Do not compile or run the Gazebo simulation module on onboard computers, nor start the legged_cheater_controller on real hardware, as it depends on simulation truth states. The real machine should start hardware interfaces, real state estimation, and legged_controller, and gradually enable targets and gains in low-risk conditions.

## Key terms

- Truth state (ground-truth state) (真值状态)
- State estimation (状态估计)
- Onboard computing (机载计算)

## Problem and symptoms

- What is the minimum compatible boundary when migrating legged_control to a custom robot?
- Why can't simulation controller and real controller be mixed?
- Direct modification of the main repository makes hardware compatibility maintenance difficult.
- Starting the real machine with the cheater controller or running Gazebo on onboard hardware causes incorrect states or resource risks.

## Environment

- ROS/ros-control; OCS2; A1; author used a 11th Gen NUC, NMPC frequency close to 200 Hz; the repository currently states it is stopped from maintenance.

## Priority diagnostics

- Check the hardware interfaces, description files, controllers, and state estimation directories against the official repository directory.

## Possible causes

- Hardware read/write interfaces and joint naming conventions do not meet framework assumptions.
- Using simulation truth states or simulation load in real machine processes.

## Attempts

- Inherit LeggedHW and implement read()/write() functions.
- Follow the pattern of unitree_description to generate URDF and maintain joint/link naming conventions.
- Start the real machine only with real state estimation and legged_controller.

## Effective fixes

- Isolate platform differences via ros-control, and separate simulation from hardware in official startup order.

## Result

- The official README lists multiple labs running on A1, with historical records of 2 hours to 1 day; the author's code structure is consistent with the repository.

## Limitations

- The repository is no longer maintained; versions, dependencies, and safety boundaries must be re-verified against the current fork.

## Safety notes

- The official README explicitly states that real machines cannot start the cheater controller; initial control should use a cradle, low gain, limit force, and emergency stop.

## Image and visual evidence

- The main framework diagram shows the trajectory trajectory → NMPC → WBC → forward force torque + low gain PD, and IMU/actuator states → Kalman filter; the repository README text is consistent with this.

## Applicability boundary

- Applicable to legged_control; other frameworks should explicitly define the boundary between simulation truth states and real measured states.
